title: Extend coproduct preservation through small nonzero support
statement: Let $D,C$ be preadditive categories [def-weil-preadditive-category], and suppose that every morphism set of $D$ is $s$-small, meaning equivalent to a type in universe $s$. Let $F:D\to C$ preserve zero morphisms. If $F$ preserves coproducts indexed by every type in universe $s$, then for every universe $v$ and every type $I$ in universe $v$, $F$ preserves every existing $I$-indexed coproduct. No existence of all such larger coproducts is asserted.

proof.text: For a coproduct B of K_i construct p_i:B→K_i by the universal property, with identity on K_i and zero on all other summands. The endomorphisms p_i followed by the ith inclusion are distinct for nonzero summands: equality for distinct i,j, tested by inclusion i and projection i, would make id(K_i)=0. The nonzero indices inject into End(B), so are s-small.

Restrict the cofan to nonzero indices. It is still colimiting: extend any family of maps by zero on zero summands and use the original universal property; maps from a zero object are unique. Shrink the support to universe s and reindex by its discrete equivalence. The hypothesis now preserves this coproduct.

Since F preserves zero morphisms it sends zero objects to zero objects. Restore the omitted zero summands in the image cofan. Its colimit property follows from uniqueness of maps out of each zero summand and the preserved restricted cofan. This proves preservation for the original existing coproduct, also for empty support.
